query: Reported superconducting high-entropy alloys are dominated by Nb-Ta matrices, while other studies concern titanium-rich systems based on heavy transition metals and partly ordered systems. Consequently, these precedents do not establish what controls superconductivity in high-entropy alloys outside the best-studied material classes. Within the defining constraint of a solid solution containing at least five elements at no less than 5 atomic percent each, what governs superconducting behavior in such an uncharacterized high-entropy alloy, and why? State one testable mechanistic hypothesis, a controlled comparison against the starting material, predicted observations relative to the baseline, applicable boundary conditions, the earlier evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In titanium‐rich high-entropy alloys based on heavy transition metals, the superconducting behavior is primarily governed by an enhanced electronic density of states at the Fermi level arising from increased hybridization of Ti d-orbitals with the heavy element d-states. This enhanced DOS boosts the electron–phonon coupling that drives superconductivity, and its effect supersedes disorder-induced suppression.
generation.material_initial_state: A homogeneous single-phase bcc high-entropy alloy that meets the solid-solution criterion (at least five elements each ≥5 at.%), formulated with a higher Ti content together with heavy transition metals (e.g., Ti-Zr-Hf-Mo plus a reduced fraction of Nb/Ta)
generation.intervention: Systematically vary the titanium content (and adjust related heavy transition-metal concentrations) relative to a Nb–Ta dominant baseline while maintaining random elemental distribution and high configurational entropy
generation.conditions: Samples synthesized under conditions ensuring a single-phase bcc (or similarly simple) structure at ambient pressure; low-temperature measurements (below 10 K) are performed to determine superconducting parameters
generation.structural_mediator: The local electronic structure near EF – specifically the d-band hybridization between Ti and heavy transition elements – which modulates the density of states
generation.mechanism: Increased Ti concentration promotes a stronger overlap of its d-orbitals with those of heavy metals, raising the density of states at the Fermi level and enhancing the electron–phonon coupling parameter. This more efficient pairing mechanism elevates Tc despite the presence of significant chemical disorder.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to Nb–Ta dominant HEAs, titanium-rich variants will exhibit a higher density of states around EF, as evidenced by increased specific heat coefficients and stronger electron–phonon coupling constants. This will manifest in an increased superconducting transition temperature (Tc) up to an optimal Ti fraction; beyond that point, excessive disorder or phase instabilities might reverse this trend.
generation.baseline: Nb–Ta dominated HEAs where superconductivity appears governed mainly by the overall electron count with limited sensitivity to additional modulation of the density of states via d-orbital hybridization
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is expected to hold for HEAs retaining a disordered, single-phase, high-symmetry structure (such as bcc) where local d-orbital hybridization controls the electronic DOS near EF. It may not apply if phase separation, ordering, or structural transitions occur, or if extreme disorder localizes electronic states.
generation.uncertainty: While evidence from Nb0.34Ti0.33Zr0.14Ta0.11Hf0.08 (PMC10489023) and the film studies supporting DOS-related Tc variations (PMC9329343) suggest the key role of electronic structure, there is uncertainty regarding the quantitative relationship between Ti content, DOS enhancement, and Tc gain in systems with heavy transition metals and possibly partly ordered structures. Our proposal extends these ideas to titanium-rich HEAs – a regime not yet fully explored.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a series of high-entropy alloys with compositions in the system Nb_xTi_yZr_aTa_bHf_c (with fixed total atomic percent and all elements ≥5%) in which the Ti content is systematically increased relative to Nb/Ta. Ensure phase homogeneity (bcc or similar simple lattice) by careful processing. Measure superconducting transition temperature (Tc), specific heat (to extract the electronic specific heat coefficient and thus the DOS at EF), and perform tunneling spectroscopy or ARPES (if feasible) to directly probe the DOS. Additionally, characterize the electron–phonon coupling via penetration depth and magnetization measurements.
measurements: XRD and SEM/EDS for phase purity and homogeneity
Low-temperature resistivity and magnetization to determine Tc and superconducting critical fields
Specific heat measurements to extract the electronic specific heat coefficient (γ) indicating DOS at EF
Tunneling spectroscopy or ARPES to map the DOS near the Fermi level
Measurements of penetration depth to infer electron–phonon coupling strength
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If, upon increasing the Ti content, the measured DOS at EF and electron–phonon coupling do not correlate with an increased Tc relative to the Nb–Ta baseline – or if enhanced Ti concentrations lead instead to a Tc suppression due primarily to disorder effects – then the hypothesis that enhanced d-orbital hybridization (and thus increased DOS) governs superconductivity in these titanium-rich HEAs would be falsified.

cited_evidence.text: The structural and physical properties of the new titanium- and niobium-rich type-A high-entropy alloy (HEA) superconductor Nb0.34Ti0.33Zr0.14Ta0.11Hf0.08 (in at.%) were studied by X-ray powder diffraction, energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, magnetization, electrical resistivity, and specific heat measurements. In addition, electronic structure calculations were performed using two complementary methods: the Korringa–Kohn–Rostoker Coherent Potential Approximation (KKR-CPA) and the Projector Augmented Wave (PAW) within Density Functional Theory (DFT). The results obtained indicate that the alloy exhibits type II superconductivity with a critical temperature close to 7.5 K, an intermediate electron–phonon coupling, and an upper critical field of 12.2(1) T. This finding indicates that Nb0.34Ti0.33Zr0.14Ta0.11Hf0.08 has one of the highest upper critical fields among all known HEA superconductors.

We recently developed superconducting HEA-type compounds, in which one of the crystallographic sites is alloyed with the criterion similar to HEAs. Since compounds with two or more crystallographic sites have unique chemical bonds, various (novel) effects of the introduction of HEA site to electronic and structural properties would be expected, which is so-called cocktail effect in the field of HEAs. In the layered BiS2-based superconductor RE(O,F)BiS2, the rare-earth site (RE) was alloyed with five different RE elements, and the improvement of superconducting properties (bulk nature of superconductivity) with increasing ΔSmix was observed. Tc was not affected by ΔSmix, and therefore its insensitivity to ΔSmix in the BiS2-based superconductor is explained using a two-dimensional structure, since similar insensitivity was also observed in an RE123 cuprate with an HEA-type RE site. In contrast, Tc of NaCl-type metal telluride, which is the target phase of this study, shows that its sensitivity to ΔSmix of HEA-type systems is larger than that of metal tellurides with one or two constituent elements at the metal site,. High-entropy alloys (HEAs) are a new type of alloy with five or more chemical elements arranged on a pseudocrystalline lattice. A high mixing-entropy minimizes the Gibbs free-energy and facilitates their crystallization on simple lattice structures, such as body-centered cubic (bcc) structure,,,. Despite the significant amount of compositional disorder, a subset of the HEAs enters a type-II superconducting phase at cryogenic temperatures,. Their large critical fields combined with superior mechanical and thermal properties render HEA promising candidates for materials applications under extreme conditions, for the fabrication of superconducting magnets, and for superconducting devices based on HEA thin films. Ongoing materials synthesis efforts have extended the family of known superconducting HEAs and developed a phenomenological understanding of their properties,. Various analyses of the upper critical field Hc2 and heat capacity measurements as a function of temperature T support a conventional Bardeen–Cooper–Schrieffer (BCS) pairing mechanism,,, with intermediate-strong coupling.
